content:
<Rep. Jared Huffman>: H.R. 2462, the ``Black Vulture Relief Act of 2025,'' is an unnecessary piece of legislation that would undermine the Migratory Bird Treaty Act and violate our treaty obligations with Mexico by removing federal protections from black vultures.\1\ This bill creates a ``solution'' in search of a problem, ignoring the fact that effective management tools for livestock producers are already readily available and working successfully.
\1\United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS). ``Migratory Bird Treaty Act of 1918''. Last visited on July 9, 2025.
The legislation addresses a non-existent crisis. The enacted 2024 America's Conservation Enhancement Reauthorization Act\2\ provides livestock producers with comprehensive access to lethal and non-lethal black vulture management tools through an efficient permit system.\3\ Fish and Wildlife Service data clearly show that permit availability has consistently outpaced demand in every state since the program's inception. In Tennessee, farmers can obtain permits within just a few days at no cost through the Farm Bureau, demonstrating that the current system works effectively.\4\\5\
\2\The Wildlife Society. ``America's Conservation Enhancement Reauthorization Act'' December 26, 2024.
\3\(Pub. L. 116-188, title I, Sec.  103, Oct. 30, 2020, 134 Stat. 911; Pub. L. 118-198, title I, Sec.  102, Dec. 23, 2024, 138 Stat. 2678.)
\4\Brandon, Hembree. Farm Progress. Black vultures: How Tennessee deals with them (June 13, 2018).
\5\Ward, Mindy & McMurtry, Dan. Farm Progress. ``USDA wildlife biologist answers 5 questions about black vultures'' (June 14, 2024).
H.R. 2462 would remove critical safeguards by granting unlimited authorization for livestock producers to ``take'' black vultures based on vague ``reasonable belief'' standards. The bill fails to specify how many birds can be killed, what constitutes ``reasonable belief,'' or how violations will be enforced. This would create a regulatory free-for-all that could lead to widespread killing of protected migratory birds based solely on speculation rather than documenting the number of birds that can be killed and what constitutes a threat.
Black vultures play an essential ecological role by cleaning up carcasses and limiting disease spread. With a stable population of 1.3 million individuals,\6\ these birds are protected under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act for good reason. Conflicts with livestock typically occur due to poor management practices, such as failing to properly dispose of carcasses or keeping vulnerable animals away from human activity.
\6\Birdful. ``How rare is a Black Vulture?''. Last accessed on July 9, 2025.
This legislation sets a dangerous precedent for Congressional interference in science-based wildlife management. When current permits exceed demand across all states, the logical response should be to maintain existing programs, not abandon protections entirely. The argument that farmers need more than the current ten-bird annual limit ignores the reality that most producers aren't even using their full allocation under existing permits.
By removing federal oversight and violating international treaty obligations, H.R. 2462 threatens to transform reasonable wildlife management into unregulated killing. Rather than advancing this unnecessary legislation, Congress should support existing programs that successfully balance legitimate agricultural needs with species protection.
H.R. 2462 represents a dangerous step toward dismantling the Migratory Bird Treaty Act and sets a precedent for removing protections from other species whenever economic interests claim inconvenience, regardless of scientific evidence or conservation necessity.
Jared Huffman,
Ranking Member.
